### 1. Scene
A rice-based meal with two thick slices resembling vegetable-studded meatloaf, several browned skin-on fish pieces, and a little cooked greenery. The protein identification is somewhat uncertain.

### 2. Vessel
A large square dinner plate, approximately 27 cm across. Using an equivalent round diameter of **26 cm**, its estimated usable area is:
**3.14 × 13² = 531 cm²**.

### 3. Items
- Cooked rice, possibly lightly seasoned
- Two vegetable-studded minced-meat loaf slices
- Browned skin-on fish pieces
- Small amounts of cooked green vegetables  
No separately measurable sauce or oil is visible; any cooking fat is included in the energy estimates.

### 4–7. Area, volume, weight, and energy
Areas are assigned without double-counting overlapping foods. Bulk density is the only volume-to-weight reduction.

| Item | Plate area | Area × average height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Rice | 40% | 212 × 1.8 = 382 ml | 0.8 | 306 g | 135 | 413 kcal |
| Meatloaf-like slices | 23% | 122 × 1.3 = 159 ml | 0.95 | 151 g | 220 | 332 kcal |
| Skin-on fish pieces | 9% | 48 × 1.5 = 72 ml | 0.95 | 68 g | 220 | 150 kcal |
| Cooked green vegetables | 4% | 21 × 1.0 = 21 ml | 0.6 | 13 g | 35 | 5 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 40 + 23 + 9 + 4 = **76% of the plate**.

### 8. Sanity check
Approximately **540 g and 900 kcal** is plausible for this substantial rice pile and thick protein portions. The small amount of greenery contributes only about 13 g. The largest uncertainty is the composition and cooking method of the protein items.
